text: MASTERPLAN v3 · BPML · SIMPLE, WITH PROOFS · 2026-08-13

items: masterplan v3 — supersedes v2 in place
goal: agents fast at writing and editing papers
every claim below carries its meter

content.value: BPML is a readable, strict markup that carries the same information as a paper's blocks. That one property gives everything else: a paper can be a file, an edit can be a diff, and every mistake can teach. Four small pieces of work; every claim measured.

items.label: denser than block JSON
items.body: Measured: the identical example paper is 504 bytes in BPML, 1,034 as blocks JSON. The saving repeats on every read and every write.

items.label: cheaper edits via derived ops
items.body: Measured on this plan's own history: op batches of 0.7–3.1KB did what full republishes of 13–51KB were doing.

items.label: publish retries collapsed
items.body: Observed: three sequential 409s (slug, description, tags) that one validate-all reply would have taught at once.

items.label: server endpoints, total
items.body: Vocabulary on /v1/capabilities and validate-all. Everything else below the API line already exists.

caption: The whole system. Right of the API, nothing changes.

content.value: No logic, no variables, no loops: BPML is a second spelling of the block tree, so blocks → BPML → blocks round-trips byte-equal (pinned by a CI property test). Strict everywhere — unknown tags and misplaced elements are teaching errors — and free inside the fence: a <demo> island carries sandboxed raw HTML with a declared fallback for email and TUI. Freedom is a block, not a loophole.

blocks.title: Why untrained agents won't get lost

content.value:
HTML priors are the asset; the design makes them mostly correct and always correctable. Naming law: when HTML has a name for it, BPML uses HTML's name (

,

,

    ,
    ); new tags name what the reader shows (, ). Wrong priors teach in one round:
    → 'no generic containers — use
    '; class= → 'BPML carries no styling'. Every pull prints canonical BPML, so agents few-shot themselves during normal work. And confusion is metered, not guessed: the unknown-tag error log drives vocabulary decisions, and the ≥90% first-try kill criterion is the confusion meter.

title: Proofs — every claim with its meter

rows.value: The identical paper above, both encodings, bytes
This plan's own edit history: 6 op batches vs the full payloads they replaced
Observed publish-wall session: violations surfaced one 409 at a time
Shipped code: portable_doc/from_markdown.ex (GFM→blocks, fail-soft) and html_sanitizer.ex
parser+printer is the same species — no new architecture
Construct map: tag↔type, attribute↔scalar key, children↔content/blocks, CDATA↔opaque value
isomorphic by construction; CI property test keeps it that way
This paper's revisions: 6 atomic op batches applied under ifRev, zero conflicts, zero losses
the write path needs nothing new

blocks.value:
.barkpark/
  papers/
    deploy-status.bpml         <- slug = filename
  state.json                   <- tool-owned: slug -> {server, dataset, rev}

pull   server blocks -> file            (Studio edits are drift; pull absorbs them)
status id-keyed diff, both directions
push   diff -> derived op batch, ifRev  (conflicts surface; nothing silently lost)

content.value: A .bpml file is a checkout, not a fork — the server stays the only source of truth. Agents edit files with their native tools; push derives the ops. Nobody hand-writes an op again.

steps.title: W0 · Contract — vocabulary + constraints on GET /v1/capabilities; validate-all on publish and patch. Two endpoints, valuable regardless of everything else.
W1 · BPML — parser + printer beside FromMarkdown; GET ?format=bpml; publish accepts BPML. Gate: the round-trip property test.
W2 · Ergonomics — ops accept BPML fragments; bp speaks BPML; agent docs teach: read BPML, patch ops, never republish.
W3 · Working copy — bp paper pull / status / diff / push over .barkpark/.

blocks.title: Kill criterion — written before the first line of code

content.value: At one month of real agent use: first-try publish ≥90% and median edit ≤2KB — or retire BPML, keep the two endpoints, write the debrief. Sunk cost: days. Deliberately unbuilt, forever unless proven needed: client runtimes, codegen toolchains, npm packages, custom file syntax.
